newsitem.title: USA: Triton Systems' IPO terms reduced - underwriter.
newsitem.headline: Triton Systems' IPO terms reduced - underwriter.

text.p: The size of Triton Systems Inc's initial public offering has been scaled back to three million shares at $9 each, according to lead underwriter Montgomery Securities.
The maker of automated teller machines had initially planned to offer 4.2 million shares between $11 and $13 a share.

The deal, filed in January, has been in the pipeline for a while now and has repeatedly been pushed back amid unfavorable market conditions. Montgomery said it now hopes to price it late on Tuesday for trading on Wednesday.

The reduced terms weren't "bringing any heat to the deal," said Vincent Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald. "It's not priced to sell at a premium," he said, adding the caveat that in the current lackluster environment for IPOs, very few deals were commanding premiums worth speaking of.
Manish Shah of the IPO Maven said that while market conditions were putting a damper on the deal's debut, he liked the company and expected it to do well in the longer term.
"Overall, it's a nice business," he said. "They have a good niche ... and a nice revenue model."
However, he said, if investors were looking for a quick return in a three to six month time frame, "that's not going to happen."

Triton's main business is the design, manufacture and sale of focused-function automated teller machines, also known as cash dispensers. These perform all of the functions typically associated with conventional ATMs, other than the accepting of deposits.
Its machines are intended to operate profitably at lower transaction volumes than conventional ATMs, the company says in its prospectus.
Triton also makes financial hardware products such as scrip terminals - countertop ATMs that provide a voucher redeemable for cash, ATM demonstration machines and card activators.

According to its filing, the Long Beach, Miss.-based company had net sales of $41 million in 1996, up from $21 million in 1995. Income from operations rose to $14.4 million from $7.4 million in the same period.
